DINA C. PASCUAL Municipal Indigenous People Mandatory Representative Municipality of Dr. Jose P. Rizal Province of Palawan Dear Hon. Pascual: This refers to your letter dated 16 August 2024, seeking for legal opinion on the following matters: 1. Are there any specific guidelines issued by the Department of the Interior and Local Government that govern the selection of IPMRs in Local Government Units (LGUs), in addition to those prescribed by the National Commission on Indigenous People (NCIP)? 2. Is it legally permissible to proceed with implementation of projects with Ancestral Domains without securing the free, prior, informed consent of the Indigenous Cultural Communities / Indigenous Peoples (ICCs / IPs), provided that the project proponent has obtained a resolution of endorsement from the concerned As to your first query, we answer in the affirmative. At the onset, we deem it prudent to highlight that under Section 446(a) of republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 " (LGC), legislative body of the municipality shall be composed of the municipal vice-mayor as the presiding officer, the regular sanggunian members, the president of the municipal chapter of the liga ng mga barangay, the president of the pambayang pederasyon ng mga sangguniang kabataan, and the sectoral representatives, as members. Correspondingly, Section 446(b) of the LGC categorically provides that sectoral representatives shall be from the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, or disabled persons. Accordingly, this Department has issued Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2010-119 entitled: "Mandatory Representation of Indigenous Cultural Communities or Indigenous Peoples in Policy-Making Bodies and Other Local Legislative Councils", dated 20 October 2010. "Matino. Mahusay at Maaasahan" -runkline No. (02) 8876 3454

MC No. 2010-119 was issued pursuant to Section 161 of Republic Act No. 8371 or the Indigenous Peoples Rights otherwise known as "The Indigenous Peoples Rights Act of 1997" (IPRA), which recognizes the policy of the State of affording indigenous people communities, adequate representations in the local government sanggunians at all levels. Said MC reiterates the Implementing Rules and Regulations of IPRA that the ICCs/lPs shall be provided mandatory representations in all policymaking bodies and in local legislative councils. The ICCs/lPs representation shall be proportionate to their population, and shall have the same prvileges as the regular members of the legislative bodies and/or policy making bodies. In addition, it emphasizes the qualification and selection process for ICC/IP representatives in local legislative bodies as embodied in NCIP Administrative Order No. 001 , series of 2009, titled, National Guidelines for the Mandatory Representation of Indigenous Peoples in Local Legislative Councils. For your reference, DILG MC No. 2010-119 dated 20 October 2010 is herein attached. As to the second query, we would like to establish that the matter falls squarely with the mandate and technical expertise of the NCIP. In this regard, we deem it proper to defer to their opinion, in view of our internal rules, as provided in Memorandum Circular No. 2010-02, which states that this Department is proscribed to act on queries that are cognizable by other agencies of the government. Be that as it may, for purposes of academic discussion, the IPRA states that indigenous concept of ownership sustains the view that ancestral domains and all resources found therein shall serve as the material bases of their cultural integrity. The indigenous concept of ownership generally holds that ancestral domains are the ICC's/lP's private but community property which belongs to all generations and therefore cannot be sold, disposed or destroyed. It likewise covers sustainable traditional resource rights2, and that right of ownership and possession of the ICCs/lPs, to their ancestral lands shall be recognized and protected3. It outlines the obligations of the State to recognize and promote all the rights of ICCs and IPs and protect their rights to their ancestral domains to ensure their economic, social and cultural wellbeing. Pertinently, the IPRA defines the free prior and informed consent as the consensus of all members of the ICCs/lPs to be determined in accordance with their respective customary laws and practices, free from any external manipulation, interference and coercion, and obtained after fully disclosing the intent and scope of the activity, in a language and process understandable to the community. Thus, the IPRA empowers the ICCs/lPs the right to halt or suspend projects that do not satisfy the consultation process required by the law. Section 16. Right to Participate in Decision -Making. - ICCs/lPs have the right to participate fully, if they so choose, at all levels of decision- making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them as well as to maintain and develop their own indigenous political structures. Consequently, the State shall ensure that the ICCs/lPs shall be given mandatory representation in policy-making bodies and other local legislative councils 2 Section 5, IPRA. 3 Section 8, IPRA. Page 2 of 3

In view of the foregoing, we are of the position that securing the free and informed consent of the ICCs/IPs must first be secured before proceeding with implementation of projects within ancestral domains, as the free, prior, and informed consent of ICCs/IPs is required for the exploration, development and use of natural resources and policies affecting Indigenous people, among others. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, B H AUTHORITY OF T CRETARY: AN VI TOR R. EDSA, Dilimar Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY October 20. 2010 MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 2010-119 TO SUBJECT ALL PROVINCIAL GOVERNORS, CITY MAYORS, MUNICIPAL MAYORS, PUNONG BARANGAYS, DILG REGIONAL DIRECTORS, THE REGIONAL GOVERNOR OF THE AVTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO, AND OTHERS CONCERNED MANDATORY REPRESENTATION OF INDIGENOUS CULTURAL COMMUNITIES OR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN POLICY-MAKING BODIES AND OTHER LOCAL LEGISLATIVE COUNCILS Pursuant to Section 16 of Republic Act No. 8371 or the Indigenous Peoples Rights Act Of 1997, quote: "ICCs/lPs have the right to participate fully, if they so choose, at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them as well as to maintain and develop their Own indigenous political structures. Consequently, the State shall ensure that the ICCs/lPs shall be given mandatory representation in policy-making bodies and other local legislative councils." In addition, Section 6, Part l, Rule IV of the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples Administrative Order NO. 1, series of 1998, or the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 8371 provides that the ICCs/lPs shall be provided mandatory representation in all policymaking bodies and in local legislative councils. ICCs/Ps representation shall be proportionate to their population, and shall have the same privileges as the regular members of the legislative bodies and/or policy making bodies. The qualification and selection processes for ICC/IP representative in local legislative bodies are embodied in NCIP Administrative Order No. 001, series of 2009. titled. National Guidelines for the Mandatory Representation Of Indigenous Peoples in Local Legislative Councils, as follows: A. Coverage (Section 5, Title l, Preliminary Provisions . NCIP AO No. 001, s., 2009) All ICCs/lPs residing with the ancestral domains Or resettled communities within the political jurisdiction or boundaries of concerned LGUs may be represented in the local legislative councils of the LGUs exercising jurisdiction over the area. However, in cases where an ancestral domain or resettled community is overlapped by two (2) or more political boundaries of LGUs, only the members of the ICCs/lPs whose residence are covered by the concerned LGU may take part in the selection of IPs mandatory representative for the said LGU. B. Minimum Qualifications (Section 9, Title II, NCIP AO No. 001, s. , 2009) The following shad be the minimum requirements for one to qualify as ICC/IP representative in the local legislative councils: (a) Natural-born Filipino citizen; (b) Registered voter in the barangay, municipality. city, province, Or district where he or she intends to assume office; (c) Bona fide ICC/IP by blood or Consanguinity: (d) Acknowledged leader of the ICCs/lPs of which he or she is a member; (e) NCIP certified as continuously engaged in ICCS' IPs in a given LGU: (f) Abie to read and write; and

(g) Knowledgeable of, and practices the customary ways of the ICCs IPs of which he/she is a member. c. Disqualifications (Section 10, Title II,NCIP AO No. 001, s., 2009) Any person suffering from or characterized by any one Of the following circumstances shall not be eligible to represent the ICCs/lPs: (a) Convicted by final judgment by the council of elders ot concerned ICCs/lPs for violating their customs and traditions: (bj Sentenced by final judgment for an offense involv,ng moral turpitude or for an offense punishable by one year or more of ilnprisonment. within two (2) years after serving sentence; (c) Removed from office as a result Of administrative case: (d) Convicted by final judgment for violating the oath of allegiance to the Republic Of-the Philippines: (e) Possession of dual citizenship; (f) Fugitive from justice, inside or outside the country: (g) Permanent resident in a foreign country or has acquired the right to reside abroad and continues to avail Ot the same right: ard (h) Insane or feeble-minded based on the findings of competent authorities. D. Term of and Removal from Office (Section 11, Title II, NCIP AO No. 001, s. , 2009) The term of office of the ICC/ IP mandat01b representative in the local legislative councils shall be for a period ot three years from the date of assumption to office and can be re-indorsed for another term by the ICCs/lPs constituents but in no case shall the representative Serve for mote than three (3) consecutive terms. For LGUs with more than one i 1 ' ICCs/lPs residing within its jurisdiction. all ICCs/IPs tribes in said LGU may agree on a term-sharing agreement based on population ratio, or on whatever local arrangement they may deem suited and applicable to address the cultural peculiarities in that LGIJ. The ICC/IP mandatory representative can be replaced anytime by the ICCsilPs who selected him/her to the position in accordance with their local guidelines on recall or removal from office. E. Selection and Assumption to Office (Section 12, Title II,NCIP AO NO. 001 , s., 2009) The selection of the particular ICC/IP representative to the legislative council shall be in accordance with the Local Guidelines that the concerned iCCs/lPs shall adopt and promulgate. Assumption to office shall take place as soon as the selection process is formally certified by the concerned ACIP Regional Director. upon recommendation of the Provincial or Community Service Center Head, as the case may be, in accordance with Administrative Order NO. OCI , s.. 2009, and the person chosen takes the appropriate oath before an authonzed officer and informs the appropriate body of his or her assumption. Powers, Duties and Functions (Section 8, Title II, NCIP AO NO. 001, s. , 2009) F. The powers, duties and functions of an ICC,'IP mandatory representative shall be the same as that Of the regular members of local legislative councils as provided in the Local Government Code of 1991. and other applicable laws. However, ICC/IP mandatory representatives shall focus on the representation of the collective interests Of ICCs/lPs; ensure support for the sustained constitution and operations Of the IPCB in their respective areas of jurisdiction; and maintain the development and practice of ICCs/lPs traditional leadership titles and structures. justice systems, conflict resolution institutions. and peace building mechanisms and processes that are compatible with the national legal system and with internationally recognized human rights.

G. Compensation and Benefits (Section 11, Title II,NCIP AO No. 001, s. , 2009) Compensation, benefits and other emoluments oi the ICC/ IP representative shall be the same with that Of the regular members ot the concerned legislative bodies as prescribed in RA 7160 and other applicable laws. In view of thc above, all Local Chief Executives are hereby directed to strictly observe the mandate Of Republic Act No. 8371, specifically, ICC,' IP mandatory replesentaticn in the local sanggunian, in accordance with the National Guidelines for the Mandatory Representation of Indigenous Peoples in Local Legislative Council, as embodled in this Circular. All DILG Regional Directors and the Regional Covet nov are ditected to cause the immediate and widest dissemination of this Memorandum Clrc.illar to all local government units within their regional jurisdictions, and to ptovide technical assistance to local government units. if necessary.
